title: Xiaomi store - Conflict of Privacy Permissions, android.permission.MY_READ_INSTALLED_PACKAGES
body: - [x] I have read the [Getting Started](https://inappwebview.dev/docs/intro/) section - [x] I have already searched for the same problem ## Environment | Technology | Version | |-----------------| ------------- | | Flutter version | 3.3.8 | | Plugin version | [6.0.0-beta.21](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_inappwebview/versions/6.0.0-beta.21) | | Android version | 10 | | iOS version | | | macOS version | | | Xcode version | | Device information: xiaomi mix3 ## Description Thank you so much for developing this flutter library. Overall performance is better than `webview_flutter`. But I have a problem when submitting the app to the app market (Xiaomi App Store). They run a security scan on the application and check that the application gets the list of installed applications at startup (android.permission.MY_READ_INSTALLED_PACKAGES). In Xiaomi's view, it is an act of disrespecting user privacy to perform such an operation before the user agrees to the application privacy policy. So they refuse to pass my app. So I would like to ask if it is possible to let WebView be initialized when it is actually used, or provide a method for developers to initialize manually. **Expected behavior:** Do not get the list of installed applications when the application starts **Current behavior:** When the app starts, when the user has not agreed to the privacy policy, get the list of installed apps immediately ## Steps to reproduce 1. This 2. Than that 3. Then

comments.body:
I don't have any `android.permission.MY_READ_INSTALLED_PACKAGES` in my android manifest file.
Just check it:
- version 6: https://github.com/pichillilorenzo/flutter_inappwebview/blob/master/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml
- version 5: https://github.com/pichillilorenzo/flutter_inappwebview/blob/v5.7.2%2B2/android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml

I don't see why the delay initialization should fix it. My plugin doesn't use it.

Maybe, is it related to https://github.com/pichillilorenzo/flutter_inappwebview/issues/1371 ?

comments.author: Participant 4
Participant 5
comments.body:
> I could implement something like @shirne has already done, but before doing that, I would like to try another way, using a "lazy" initialization for the Cookie Manager and the other classes.

We don't have to call `init` explicitly if the method is done when the first controller is constructing, using flags to indicate could be better IMO.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: I have solved the current problem through your means. Thank you very much @hellohejinyu

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: You don't need to call any `init` method or whatever. The android classes will be initiated when you will call native methods the first time, such as `CookieManager.getCookies`, etc.
